authority: Owner requested continued quality fixes, careful planning and replanning; integrate the accepted local fixes after the Windows predecessor is merged, preserving every original branch and worktree.
bounded_units: U1 Integrate accepted batch, depth and shear commits onto the exact merged Windows base without rewriting history.
U2 Retain both session histories and task boundaries; reconcile recurrence deltas from the common base and regenerate the current integration handoff.
U3 Freeze and format once, then run full Python, full FastAPI and repository checks as the named cumulative gate.
U4 Independently audit exact candidate, verify integrity once, publish one PR and merge only unchanged reviewed head with passing required hosted checks.
acceptance_rows: I01 Batch requested engineering inputs reach single-beam evaluation; genuine failed checks remain failures.
I02 Passing combined results bind generated longitudinal depths and every stirrup zone to the accepted strength basis; coherent BBS remains usable.
I03 Every Windows CSharp/source-evidence path outside the four shared planning records remains byte-identical to the merged predecessor.
I04 Both session histories and Windows next-step boundaries survive; recurrence events are counted once from the common base.
I05 Cumulative tests, exact-head independent review, integrity, required hosted checks and candidate/merge tree equality have retained evidence.
non_goals: No further quality units, new formulas, automatic redesign, Windows implementation changes, installed acceptance claims, release, or branch/worktree cleanup.

verification.cumulative: Full Python package suite, full FastAPI suite and canonical 32 repository checks once after content freeze; rerun only affected repair evidence if necessary.
verification.review: Independent exact-head main-outcome and integration audit, followed by one read-only candidate-integrity run.
verification.hosted: Single PR for entire stacked milestone; required checks must pass on unchanged reviewed head before merge.
